🚨🇲🇽 <u>PENTAGON PLANS "LAND STRIKES" ON LATAM CARTELS — MEXICO NAMED</u>

Mexico just got its most explicit threat yet from Washington: US War Secretary Pete Hegseth said the Pentagon plans to attack drug traffickers "on land" in Latin America, vowing to eradicate them "from cocaine trafficking to fentanyl in the plazas of Mexico." President Sheinbaum's position hasn't moved: coordination, yes — subordination and foreign boots on Mexican soil, never. The same Pentagon whose boat strikes have killed at least 215 people in the Caribbean and Pacific now wants to bring that campaign ashore.

🇲🇽💻 <u>KIO DATA CENTERS BETS UP TO $1.3 BILLION ON MEXICO'S AI BOOM</u>

El Economista reports that Mexico's KIO Data Centers completed phases two and three of its QRO2 mega campus in Querétaro — $170 million invested — with another $200 million coming this year for CDMX, Monterrey and Querétaro. Next: up to $1.3 billion by 2030 for QRO3, a 100 MW facility that would be the largest data center in company history, plus 8,100 jobs. Marcelo Ebrard handed KIO the "Hecho en México" seal: the AI ecosystem "is going to be the new major economic growth, and Mexico is going to be part of it."
banner: DATA CENTERS: KIO BETS $1.3B ON MEXICO

🇲🇽🎓 <u>1,437 WOMEN GRADUATE FROM CDMX'S ECONOMIC AUTONOMY PROGRAM</u>

Mexico City's Secretariat of Women graduated the first generation of its Women's Economic Autonomy Program: 1,437 participants with Ceneval-certified diplomas after two months of training in administration, digital marketing, leadership and personal finance — tools to launch their own projects or enter formal work. Under Clara Brugada the pilot became permanent policy. Coordinator María Elena Esparza: "That's what economic autonomy is about: the final goal is freedom."

🇲🇽🏭 <u>NAHLE TAKES SAN PEDRO SUGAR MILL'S FUTURE TO THE FEDERAL TABLE</u>

More than 6,000 families in Lerdo de Tejada, Veracruz depend on the San Pedro sugar mill — one of the complexes auctioned off under Vicente Fox. Governor Rocío Nahle is sitting down with Grupo Porres, the Economy Ministry and the SHCP to keep it alive, tying the rescue to the 4T's guaranteed-price policy for sugarcane. Her formula: "Dialogue, proposals, support — look everywhere."
banner: SUGAR: NAHLE FIGHTS TO SAVE SAN PEDRO MILL

🔥🇲🇽 <u>SHEINBAUM SHREDS PRI CHIEF FOR BEGGING US TO PULL VISAS FROM MEXICAN OFFICIALS</u>

PRI president 'Alito' Moreno ran to Washington to demand the US revoke visas from Mexican electoral councilors — after Mexico's own electoral authority sanctioned him. Sheinbaum: "What Mexican — imagine, president of a political party — goes and files a complaint in the United States asking them to take away visas? It's the lowest level of believing in Mexico. He no longer believes in Mexico or in Mexicans." What would PRI leaders from just 10 years ago say?
banner: SHEINBAUM: 'ALITO' BEGS US FOR VISA BANS

🇲🇽✈️ <u>MEXICO BREAKS FIVE TOURISM RECORDS IN FIRST HALF OF 2026</u>

51.1 million international travelers came to Mexico from January to June — 7.7% more than last year — including 24.5 million tourists, $18.8 billion in revenue and 6.6 million cruise passengers. All historic highs. While the usual voices sell Mexico as a "failed state," the world keeps booking flights. Sheinbaum's goal is the top 5 of global destinations: "Come to Mexico, a marvelous country — it's in fashion."

🇲🇽🥑 <u>US FULLY REOPENS MICHOACÁN AVOCADO EXPORTS — DIALOGUE BEATS ULTIMATUMS</u>

Washington suspended avocado inspections in Michoacán over "security concerns." Mexico didn't escalate or cave — it negotiated. Agriculture Secretary Columba López announced the full resumption: "Thanks to the dialogue tables and joint work between authorities of Mexico and the United States, today, August 13, inspection and export of avocados in Michoacán fully resumes." Mexico's most iconic export moves again.

🇲🇽✊ 505 years after the defense of Tenochtitlan: Mexican women still defend sovereignty. "A day like today, August 13, 505 years ago, Mexica women and men defended their city, their territory, their ways of life. Today, 505 years later, Mexican women continue defending the sovereignty of this country." — Noemí Juárez, Undersecretary of Basic Education On August 13, 1521, Tenochtitlan fell after an 80-day siege. The mañanera's "Women in History" segment honored the women of that defense and the indigenous women who preserved language and ancestral knowledge.
